paper_title: Graph of Thoughts: Solving Elaborate Problems with Large Language Models
paper_abstract: We introduce Graph of Thoughts (GoT): a framework that advances prompting capabilities in large language models (LLMs) beyond those offered by paradigms such as Chain-of-Thought or Tree of Thoughts (ToT). The key idea and primary advantage of GoT is the ability to model the information generated by an LLM as an arbitrary graph, where units of information ("LLM thoughts") are vertices, and edges correspond to dependencies between these vertices. This approach enables combining arbitrary LLM thoughts into synergistic outcomes, distilling the essence of whole networks of thoughts, or enhancing thoughts using feedback loops. We illustrate that GoT offers advantages over state of the art on different tasks, for example increasing the quality of sorting by 62% over ToT, while simultaneously reducing costs by >31%. We ensure that GoT is extensible with new thought transformations and thus can be used to spearhead new prompting schemes. This work brings the LLM reasoning closer to human thinking or brain mechanisms such as recurrence, both of which form complex networks

prior_works.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
prior_works.relationship_sentence: GoT takes CoT’s core idea of explicitly generating intermediate "thoughts" and generalizes it by representing these thoughts as vertices in a graph rather than a single linear chain.

prior_works.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
prior_works.relationship_sentence: GoT directly generalizes CoT-SC’s multi-sample generation and selection by introducing graph-level scoring and ranking functions (E and R) that evaluate and select among multiple thoughts across an arbitrary graph, not just independent chains.

prior_works.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
prior_works.relationship_sentence: GoT is proposed explicitly as a generalization of ToT’s tree-structured search, replacing rigid trees with arbitrary graphs to enable aggregation of branches and feedback loops that ToT cannot express.

prior_works.title: Large Language Model Guided Tree-of-Thought
prior_works.relationship_sentence: This ToT variant underscores the tree-based search paradigm that GoT critiques and overcomes by allowing non-tree operations like merging multiple reasoning paths and forming cycles for refinement.

prior_works.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
prior_works.relationship_sentence: GoT’s refinement transformation (graph self-loops) concretely operationalizes the Self-Refine insight that LLM outputs can be iteratively improved via feedback within the reasoning process.

prior_works.title: Plan-and-Solve Prompting: Improving Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Reasoning by Large Language Models
prior_works.relationship_sentence: The planning-plus-execution decomposition in Plan-and-Solve informed GoT’s Graph of Operations abstraction, which encodes multi-step decompositions and aggregation as DAGs rather than linear plans.

synthesis_narrative:
Chain-of-Thought (CoT) established that prompting with explicit intermediate reasoning steps markedly improves LLM performance by surfacing the model’s latent deductive traces. Self-Consistency built on this by sampling multiple CoT trajectories and selecting a final answer via aggregation of evidence, demonstrating that exploration plus selection can outperform a single chain. Tree of Thoughts (ToT) reframed reasoning as a deliberate search over a tree of partial thoughts, enabling branching, lookahead, and backtracking under BFS/DFS-style control but restricting the structure to trees. The LLM-guided ToT variant further refined search guidance yet retained the tree constraint, implicitly preventing operations like merging paths or cyclic refinements. In parallel, Self-Refine showed that iterative self-feedback can reliably improve candidates via repeated critique-and-revision, pointing to the utility of explicit refinement loops. Plan-and-Solve established the value of decomposing a problem into a plan and then solving substeps, highlighting the importance of structured multi-step decomposition and subsequent integration.
Taken together, these works reveal a gap: existing formulations either follow a single chain, multiple independent chains, or a tree, but lack a representation that supports both aggregation of disparate partial solutions and iterative refinement within one unifying formalism. Graph of Thoughts synthesizes these insights by modeling thoughts as vertices with dependency edges, extending multi-sample selection to graph-level scoring/ranking, incorporating self-refinement as loops, and encoding decompositions and merges as DAGs. This natural generalization preserves the strengths of CoT/CoT-SC/ToT while enabling novel graph-enabled transformations that improve quality and cost across tasks.

innovation_classification.reasoning: Recasts reasoning as graph search and controls exploration/selection at inference time beyond tree constraints.
